title: Two Sum: UPI Split
statement: At a chai stall you paid with two UPI payments that add up exactly to the bill. Given an array of payment amounts and the bill total, return the indices of the two payments (any order). Exactly one pair exists and you cannot reuse an element.
hints: Restate the problem in your own words. For nums = [2,7,11,15] and target 9, which indices do you return and why?
The brute force checks every pair. If you are standing on one number, what exact value are you hoping to find among the others?
A hash map answers 'have I seen this value before?' in O(1). Store each number's index as you scan, and look up target minus the current number.

title: Valid Brackets
statement: Given a string containing only ()[]{}, return true if every opener is closed by the same type of bracket, in the correct order.
hints: Walk through '([)]' by hand. Is it valid, and at which character do you first know?
Which bracket must be closed first: the oldest opener or the newest one?
The newest unmatched opener must close first, which is last-in-first-out. A stack fits: push openers, and on a closer compare it with the top.

title: Binary Search: Train Board
statement: Train numbers on a station board are sorted and distinct. Return the index of the given train number, or -1 if it is not on the board, in O(log n) time.
hints: For [1,3,5,7,9] and target 7, how many numbers would you check reading left to right? Could the sorting help you skip some?
If you look at the middle element, what does comparing it to the target tell you about which half to discard?
Binary search: keep lo and hi pointers, check mid, and move one pointer past mid each step. Watch the loop condition and off-by-one errors.

title: Maximum Subarray: Best Streak
statement: A cricketer's daily score changes (gains and losses) are in an array. Find the contiguous stretch of days with the largest total and return that total.
hints: For [-2,1,-3,4], list a few contiguous subarrays and their sums. Which is largest?
Standing at index i, the best subarray ending here either starts fresh at i or extends the one ending at i-1. When would you start fresh?
This is Kadane's algorithm: keep cur = max(nums[i], cur + nums[i]) and a separate best for the maximum seen so far.

title: Group Anagrams
target: O(n * k log k) time, O(n * k) space
statement: Given an array of strings, group the anagrams together. Return the groups in any order.
hints: What makes two words anagrams of each other? Write what 'eat' and 'tea' have in common.
If you could convert every word into a single form that is identical for all its anagrams, what would you do with that form?
Use a hash map from a canonical key (the sorted letters of the word) to the list of words that share it.

title: Number of Islands
statement: A satellite map is a grid of '1' (land) and '0' (water). Count the islands. An island is land connected horizontally or vertically.
hints: Draw the grid [[1,1,0],[0,1,0],[0,0,1]] and circle the islands. How did you decide where one ends?
When you find a land cell, how could you visit every cell connected to it so you never count that island twice?
Scan the grid; on each unvisited '1', count one island and flood-fill (DFS or BFS) its connected land, marking cells visited.

title: Blinkit: First Unique SKU
statement: During a festival sale, a Blinkit dark store scans item codes one by one. Return the index of the first item code that appears exactly once, or -1 if every code repeats.
hints: For ['milk','egg','milk','bread','egg'], which code is the first one that appears only once, and how did you check?
Checking each code against the whole list is slow. What if you counted every code in one pass first?
Pass 1: build a Map of code to count. Pass 2: walk the array again and return the first index whose count is 1.

title: Railway Platform Slots
target: O(n log n) time, O(n) space
statement: Trains reserve platform time slots as [start, end] pairs, in any order. Merge all overlapping slots and return the merged list sorted by start time. Slots that only touch, like [1,3] and [3,5], also merge.
hints: Draw [1,3], [2,6], [8,10] on a number line. Which slots overlap, and what does a merged slot look like?
If the slots were sorted by start time, which neighbour would you compare each slot with?
Sort by start. Keep a result list: if the next start is <= the last end, extend the last end with max(lastEnd, nextEnd); otherwise push a new slot.
